name: Steel Tectonics Inc
old_description: Founded in 2006 - Shawn Nelson, President of STI Machining purchased a small machine shop that was running out of a garage. There he found his love of machining, since then he has doubled the production of the business both climates and production. Operating out of an 8000 sq ft building housing half a dozen machines.
about:
Steel Tectonics Inc., doing business as STI Machining, was founded in 2006 in West Jordan, Utah, when Shawn Nelson purchased a small machine shop that had been operating out of a garage. The company remains family-run; Nelson’s two sons, Cody and Justin, are now learning the operation alongside their father, who brings more than 25 years of machining experience.

The shop specializes in high-performance plastics machining and engineering services, offering 2- to 4-axis milling and turning as well as design-for-manufacture support. Production takes place in an 8,000-square-foot facility that houses roughly half a dozen machines. The team works with a range of fluoropolymers and engineering plastics, including PFA, polypropylene, PTFE, acetal, and PVDF.

STI Machining’s primary customer base is the semiconductor industry, where its parts are used in process equipment and fluid-handling systems. The company also serves other sectors that require precision plastic components, though the input does not name additional industries.

Nelson says the firm’s edge comes from deep specialization in plastics: every employee is versed in the material’s machining challenges, and the shop has refined speed-and-feed rates to achieve consistent finishes. The operation emphasizes tight lead times and responsive communication as core service differentiators.
